ad9db43130: Why does BMI have different cut-offs for Asian populations?
744c4b9bf1: A 2004 WHO expert consultation found that many Asian populations have a higher proportion of body fat and higher risk of type 2 diabetes and heart disease at a lower BMI than European populations. It kept the international categories but proposed additional public-health action points of 23 (increased risk) and 27.5 (high risk) for Asian populations.
c5f64c9893: Why check waist-to-height ratio as well as BMI?
06a36510c4: BMI can't tell muscle from fat or show where fat is stored. Waist-to-height ratio reflects fat around the middle, which is more closely linked to heart and metabolic risk. A common guide is to keep your waist to less than half your height (a ratio below 0.5).
e2aa539988: Is the 3,500-calorie rule accurate for weight loss?
27769bf416: Only as a rough starting point. The idea that a 3,500-calorie deficit always removes one pound of fat assumes your energy use stays constant, but it falls as you lose weight, so loss usually slows over time. Treat any weight-loss timeline as an estimate and adjust it from your actual progress.

66045230d8: No. The calculations run in your browser and the numbers you enter aren't sent to or stored on our servers. Like most websites, the site itself uses analytics and advertising cookies — see our privacy policy for details.
